title: MIRACLE: Model-free Imitation and Reinforcement Learning for Adaptive Cut-Selection
claim: A learned agent selects a small subset of candidate actions each step in a closed loop, trained offline with a reward learned from expert demonstrations.
layout: Single panel, boxes and arrows, closed feedback loop, dashed offline-training group
description: A single flowchart of rounded boxes joined by black arrows. Blue boxes are data or artifacts: Expert Trajectories, State and Candidate Cuts, Selected Cuts, and Final Solution. Orange boxes are learned components: the GAIL Discriminator and the MIRACLE Agent (PPO policy). A dashed box labeled 'Offline Training' encloses the expert trajectories and the discriminator. An arrow runs from the dashed SCIP Environment box, labeled 'Generates', to the state and candidate cuts. From there an arrow goes to the agent, which 'Selects' cuts. A long loop at the bottom, labeled 'Apply Cuts & Re-Solve LP', returns to the environment. A second loop across the top leads to Final Solution. The discriminator sends a 'Learned Reward r_GAIL' arrow to the agent. The eye goes first to the central orange agent box and the dashed training group.
caption: MIRACLE Framework. At each step (k), the SCIP Environment, generates a state (sk) and candidate cuts (Ck). This information is processed by our trained MIRACLE Agent (πθ), which selects a small subset of cuts (ak) and applies them back into the environment. The LP is re-solved until a final solution is reached. The agent’s policy is learned offline via PPO, guided by a dense reward signal from a GAIL Discriminator trained on expert SCIP trajectories.
abstract: Mixed-Integer Programming (MIP) solvers rely heavily on cutting planes to tighten LP relaxations, but traditional approaches generate thousands of cuts that consume gigabytes of memory while providing minimal benefit. We present an intelligent cut selection framework that achieves a 98.1\% reduction in memory usage while maintaining competitive solving with an objective gap of approximately 0.08\%. Within this RL framework, we use Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) to learn a behavioral model that imitates the expert solver’s decisions. The adversarially imitated behavioral model drives an agent comprising these key innovations: (i) a cut-selection policy trained via curriculum learning; and (ii) adaptive inference that dynamically adjusts computational budgets. Through comprehensive evaluation across SetCover and diverse MIPLIB problems, we demonstrate consistent speedups (3.78$\times$ average on MIPLIB) and achieve a 100\% success rate on instances where traditional SCIP fails 47-53\% of the time. Our method also reduces peak memory consumption from 3.03GB to 46 MB, enabling optimization in previously inaccessible and other resource-constrained environments where traditional solvers face fundamental limitations.
